name: NF C 14-100 (France)
references: France's NF C 14-100 (the supply from the network to the connection breaker), as SéQuélec's guide GP 16 (December 2017, the dossier of a collective connection that Enedis and the local distributors ask) works it
note: A building's demand by this country's method (`building_demand`). The rest of the discipline comes from BIMCraft's library, and says so.

building_demand.source: France's NF C 14-100 (the supply from the network to the connection breaker), as SéQuélec's guide GP 16 (December 2017, the dossier of a collective connection that Enedis and the local distributors ask) works it: a building's power is the sum of its users' sizing powers times a weighting coefficient by the number of users downstream.

dwelling.source: GP 16, p. 6, the least sizing powers of a dwelling without electric heating, by its main rooms or its floor area

grades.name: student
grades.source: GP 16, p. 6: a student's dwelling up to 20 m², 3 kVA

grades.name: 1-2 rooms
grades.source: GP 16, p. 6: 1 or 2 main rooms or up to 35 m², 6 kVA

grades.name: 3-5 rooms
grades.source: GP 16, p. 6: 3 to 5 main rooms or 35 to 100 m², 9 kVA

grades.name: 6+ rooms
grades.source: GP 16, p. 6: 6 main rooms or more, or over 100 m², 12 kVA

diversity.source: GP 16, p. 6: the weighting coefficient by the number of users downstream, 1 up to 4 and 0.38 from 50

notes: The coefficient counts the users downstream; a user other than a dwelling at a limited power (a caretaker's flat, a shop) may be given as a group with its `demand`, so that it is weighted with the dwellings.
A declared `demand` above a grade's is taken as declared: the grades are the least, not the power asked.
not_covered: dwellings with electric heating, which GP 16 (p. 7) sizes by its own expressions of the heating power installed
installations at a watched power (over 36 kVA), which GP 16 adds at the power they need
the conductors and the voltage drops of the riser and the branches (GP 16, pp. 5 and 8)
